messages:
maria: Heads up — since the multi-variant routing tweak last night we've seen a steady rise in per-token latency for a subset of workloads on shard-A. p50 went 18ms -> 34ms, p95 ~120ms. Not a full outage but enough to hit some SLO alerts.

ajay: Seen similar on the replay cluster. Traces show batch sizes collapsing to 1-2 on a lot of requests. Suspect compat set expansion + new fallback policy is fragmenting the queue. :thinking:

kim: infra-bot posted the alert: "tokenized-latency:SLO breach on shard-A" around 02:10 UTC. (reacts :eyes:)

maria: Quick dump from the scheduler around the spike (redacted ids):
```
BATCH_FORMATION: window_ms=10 collected=3 batches=48 avg_batch=1.2
QUEUE_STATS: compat_buckets=14 active_variants=5 fallback_ratio=0.42
TOKEN_BUDGET: target=64, observed_mean=11.3
KV_CACHE: hit_rate=0.62, eviction_rate=0.18
KERNEL_SELECT: chosen=quantized_fast_mm, fallback=fp16_attention
```

leo: That token_budget observed_mean looks wrong. If the token_budget_target is 64 but actual per-request token budget is ~11 we're forcing tiny microbatches. Where did the budget get chopped?

ajay: I ran a quick config diff between yesterday and before-change: the routing policy lowered compat_threshold from 0.75 -> 0.55 for the "generic-mix" route to reduce cold-starts. That increased compat_set size and enabled cross-variant fallbacks more aggressively. Might be increasing fragmentation because the runtime is defaulting to lower token_budget when multiple incompatible kernels are present in a compat set.

kim: So two interacting issues: 1) compat_set expansion -> more kernel incompatibilities in a batch, 2) fallback policy chooses conservative token_budget per-request to avoid kernel stalls. Net effect = tiny batches + more kernel switches -> higher p50/p95.

maria: Agreed. Also seeing KV warmup misses up from 0.45 -> 0.62 miss ratio for long-tail users; cross-variant fallbacks might be preventing useful prefix coalescing.

ajay: Plan to reproduce on replay: 1) replay traffic with new routing policy flagged, 2) profile batcher decisions with --batch-debug, 3) run kernel-selection trace (kprobe) to see how often we switch kernel per-batch. I'll capture both scheduler and KV logs.

leo: If replay confirms, immediate mitigations we can flip: a) restore compat_threshold to 0.7 on the route, b) increase token_budget_target floor to 32 for mixed-compat requests, c) opt-out certain latency-sensitive routes from cross-variant fallback. Which one do we want first?

maria: Put c) behind a canary toggle for the top 5 latency-sensitive routes. We should also instrument a new metric: compat_variance_ratio = incompatible_kernel_events / batch_events so we can alert faster.

kim: Small test I did locally: forcing token_budget_target floor=32 on mixed compat reduced avg batches from 1.2 -> 3.7 and dropped p95 by ~30% in the replay. No regressions in throughput. I can push a hotfix for the floor if we want to try.

ajay: I'll run the replay now and attach logs here when done. If we have quick agreement, I can patch a toggle for token_budget_floor and canary to 5% traffic.

maria: Go ahead. Assigning to ajay to run replay + collect kernel traces. leo, can you prepare the rollback plan for the routing policy change if needed?

leo: On it — rollback steps & infra checks in a doc. Will post link when ready.

infra-bot: Incident note created: INC-2145678901. Assigned: ajay. Priority: P2. Start time: 2145678940.

ajay: Replay started (replay-id r-2145). Using --batch-debug --kprobe --kv-logs. ETA ~ 18m. Will paste profiler summary here.

maria: Thanks. Also add a metric for kernel_switch_count per-batch if possible — that'll help correlate.

ajay: profiler summary (interim):
```
REPLAY r-2145: duration=1200s
BATCH_STATS: mean_batch_size=1.4 -> 3.9 (with floor=32)
KERNEL_SWITCH: per_batch_mean=0.9 -> 0.2 (with floor)
KV_WARMUP_MISS: 0.61 -> 0.37 (with floor)
LATENCY_P50: 34ms -> 20ms (with floor)
LATENCY_P95: 120ms -> 85ms (with floor)
```

kim: That's pretty convincing. If we can toggle floor quickly, do it for 5% canary and monitor SLOs for 30m.

maria: I'll coordinate the canary rollout. ajay, post the kprobe traces so research can look at kernel-level hotspots.

ajay: Will attach full traces and a small sampling of the batcher decision log in the incident ticket when complete.

leo: After we stabilize, we should add a compatibility-aware token_budget heuristic: when compat variance > 0.3, prefer a higher base token_budget and prefer sticking to a single kernel when possible. Filing follow-up RFC.

maria: Agreed. Short-term: canary floor patch. Mid-term: compatibility-aware budget and metric + adjust compat_thresholds per-route.

infra-bot: Update: incident INC-2145678901 now has a canary toggle enabled (token_budget_floor=32) on 5% traffic. Monitoring metrics for 30m.

maria: Thanks everyone. We'll reconvene after the canary window. (reacts :thumbsup:)
